newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees '97 steel exports steady at 6.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: China sees '97 steel exports steady at 6.5 mln T.

text.p: China aims to repeat last year's record output of 100 million tonnes of steel in 1997 while exports will remain steady at about 6.5 million tonnes, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

China, which became the world's number one steel producer in 1996 with steel output rising 7.59 percent to 100.02 million tonnes, will give priority to readjusting product mix this year, it quoted officials at a national conference as saying.

The industry will pour 60 percent of total investment into increasing the number of products and improving quality, it said. It will use 27 percent of the investment to develop energy-saving technology, it said.

China will increase output of continuous casting billets by eight million tonnes in 1997 from 53.28 million tonnes in 1996, raising the ratio of continuous casting to 60 percent from 53.27 percent in 1996, it said.
The industry will try to cut production costs by two percent and save three million tons of coal, compared with the four million tonnes it saved in 1996, it said.
China will export 6.5 million tonnes of steel products and lump metal in 1997, virtually unchanged from 1996 when exports fell, it said.
Imports in 1996 increased by 15 percent to 15 million tonnes.
Total output of steel plate, piping and steel bars hit 32.53 million tonnes in 1996, a 10.7 percent increase over 1995.
The industry reported turnover of 27.3 billion yuan and a post-tax profit of 21 billion yuan in 1996, Xinhua said but gave no more details.
